name: openGym
description: Self-hosted gym & body-weight tracker — plan routines, log workouts (supersets, warm-ups, cardio), see which muscles are trained, fatigued or detrained, import from FitNotes/Strong/Hevy, passkey login. Your data, your server.
one_liner: A workout and gym-tracking app you run yourself on your own server, instead of handing your fitness history to a company's app or paying a monthly subscription for one.
buyer: A personal trainer or small boutique gym that wants to give clients a branded workout tracker without being locked into an off-the-shelf fitness SaaS.
business_use_cases: A personal trainer self-hosts it and gives each client passkey logins to a tracker built around that trainer's own programs instead of a generic app.
A privacy-conscious lifter runs it on a home server to replace a paid subscription app like Strong or Hevy, importing their existing workout history.
A boutique gym offers it as a membership perk tied to in-house programs, differentiating from chain gyms that just point members at a generic app.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a managed, white-labeled hosted version for personal trainers and small gyms who don't want to run their own server.
Sell a one-time 'migrate and set up' service for people moving off FitNotes, Strong or Hevy who want self-hosting but not the Docker work themselves.

steal_this: This weekend, host an instance for a local personal trainer's client roster and charge a small monthly fee to manage hosting, backups and updates for them.
